messages.content:
You are a clinical validator checking whether a PTSD case
vignette accurately reflects a patient's required cognitive connections.

You will receive:
- A vignette to validate
- A list of REQUIRED edges that must appear
- A list of ACTIVE components that must appear

---

COMPONENT SYNONYMS
Each component may appear by its exact name or any accepted synonym:
  Triggers            → "triggers", "reminders", "cues", "triggering stimuli"
  Negative Appraisals → "negative appraisals", "negative beliefs", "appraisals", "distorted beliefs"
  Memory              → "intrusive memory", "trauma memory", "traumatic memory", "the memory"
  Threat              → "sense of threat", "perceived threat", "threat", "feeling of danger"
  Maladaptive Strategies → "maladaptive strategies", "avoidance", "maladaptive coping", "safety behaviours"

---

CAUSAL STANDARD
A required edge A→B is SATISFIED if, within the same paragraph:
  - Both A and B (or their synonyms) appear, AND
  - The paragraph conveys — through any language — that A influences, drives, or leads to B.
This includes direct causal sentences, sequential structure, or connecting phrases
like "because of", "this meant", "so", "which led", "as a result", "consequently", "in turn".
A required edge is MISSING only if no paragraph conveys the A→B relationship at all.

---

SECTION 1 — COMPONENT CHECK
Active components (must appear in the vignette):
  - Maladaptive Strategies
  - Negative Appraisals
  - Triggers

Confirm each component appears as a described feature of the patient's presentation.
This is an internal check only — do NOT add component results to violations.

---

SECTION 2 — REQUIRED EDGES
  - Triggers → Maladaptive Strategies
  - Triggers → Negative Appraisals
  - Negative Appraisals → Triggers

For each edge, apply the causal standard above.
- If satisfied: do nothing — only failures are reported.
- If missing: add it to violations and explain in one sentence what causal relationship is absent.

Validate the following vignette against the cognitive graph.

Samantha is a 22-year-old South Eastern Asian male student who recently returned from serving as a relief worker in a war-torn country. The traumatic event that has left an indelible mark on his psyche occurred during one of the missions when he was caught between warring factions, feeling completely helpless and under constant surveillance by hostile forces. This experience has led to Samantha developing intense triggers related to being watched and the presence of authority figures in uniform. Since returning home, Samantha feels that every movement is scrutinized, and the sensation of being observed brings back vivid memories of his harrowing experiences. He finds it particularly distressing when he encounters police officers or individuals wearing military uniforms on campus. These triggers have significantly influenced his behavior, leading him to avoid social interactions with friends and classmates whom he once enjoyed spending time with before the event. The fear of feeling watched or observed has also made eye contact nearly impossible for Samantha. He avoids it entirely, as making eye contact with others often intensifies his sense of being scrutinized. This avoidance extends to any visible symbols of authority or weapons, which he tries to steer clear of at all costs. The presence of military or police uniforms evokes a flood of memories and intense anxiety, further reinforcing his maladaptive strategies. Samantha has come to believe that he has failed in his most important role in life, feeling that he was not able to protect himself or others effectively during the traumatic event. This belief is deeply intertwined with his negative appraisals about his body’s response; even though he is now safe, his body continues to react as if danger still lurks around every corner. He feels helpless and believes he cannot prevent bad things from happening to him. These negative appraisals have a profound impact on Samantha’s triggers. The belief that he has failed in his role exacerbates his fear of being watched or observed, making it even more difficult for him to engage with the world around him. His heightened sense of vulnerability and helplessness fuels his avoidance behaviors, creating a self-reinforcing cycle where each trigger reinforces his negative beliefs and vice versa. Samantha’s academic performance has suffered as a result of these struggles. He finds it increasingly challenging to attend classes or participate in group projects, often staying home to avoid the triggering environments on campus. This isolation has strained his relationships with friends, who do not fully understand what he is going through. Despite these challenges, Samantha finally decided to seek help because his daily functioning had become too compromised. What frightens him most is the possibility of never feeling safe again and being trapped in a cycle of fear and avoidance forever. He hopes that therapy can provide some relief and help him reclaim control over his life, allowing him to reconnect with others and continue his studies without constant dread.
